Autumn Equinox Harvest Grain Salad

Served at: Autumn Equinox (Mabon)

Serves 6-8Prep 25 minCook 40 min

This Autumn Equinox Harvest Grain Salad celebrates Mabon's bounty, balancing the last warmth of summer with the crisp beginnings of autumn. It features hearty grains and seasonal produce, symbolizing gratitude for the harvest and preparing for the cooler months ahead. A perfect dish for sharing at your Mabon feast.

Ingredients

  • 1 cup (180 g) farro, rinsed
  • 2 cups (480 ml) vegetable broth or water
  • 1 small (approx. 1.5 lb / 680 g) butternut squash, peeled, seeded, and diced into 1/2-inch (1.3 cm) cubes
  • 2 tablespoons olive oil, divided
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt, divided, plus more to taste
  • 1/4 teaspoon black pepper, divided, plus more to taste
  • 1/2 cup (60 g) pecans, roughly chopped
  • 1 crisp apple (e.g., Honeycrisp or Fuji), cored and diced
  • 1/2 cup (70 g) dried cranberries
  • 1/4 cup (15 g) fresh parsley, chopped
  • 3 tablespoons apple cider vinegar
  • 1 tablespoon maple syrup
  • 1 teaspoon Dijon mustard
  • 1/4 cup (60 ml) olive oil
  • Pinch of salt (for dressing)
  • Pinch of black pepper (for dressing)

Method

  1. Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
  2. In a medium saucepan, combine the rinsed farro with vegetable broth or water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 25-30 minutes, or until the farro is tender and the liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and set aside to cool slightly.
  3. While the farro cooks, toss the diced butternut squash with 1 tablespoon of olive oil, 1/4 teaspoon salt, and 1/8 teaspoon black pepper on the prepared baking sheet. Roast for 20-25 minutes, or until tender and lightly caramelized, flipping halfway through. Set aside to cool.
  4. Spread the chopped pecans on a small, dry skillet over medium heat. Toast for 3-5 minutes, stirring frequently, until fragrant. Watch carefully to prevent burning. Remove from heat and set aside.
  5. In a small bowl, whisk together the apple cider vinegar, maple syrup, and Dijon mustard for the vinaigrette. Slowly drizzle in the remaining 1/4 cup (60 ml) olive oil while whisking constantly until emulsified. Season with a pinch of salt and pepper.
  6. In a large mixing bowl, combine the cooled farro, roasted butternut squash, toasted pecans, diced apple, dried cranberries, and chopped fresh parsley.
  7. Pour the maple-cider vinaigrette over the salad ingredients. Toss gently to ensure everything is well coated.
  8. Taste and adjust seasoning (salt, pepper) if needed. Serve warm or at room temperature.

Tips

  • For added protein, stir in 1/2 cup (120 g) crumbled goat cheese or feta just before serving.
  • This salad can be made ahead of time. Store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Add extra fresh parsley just before serving if desired.
  • Experiment with other grains like quinoa, wild rice, or barley, adjusting cooking times as needed.
